upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

This is the key determining factor for your eligibility:

- Alex has been in hospital/residential accommodation for more than 12 weeks (15 weeks)
- Normally, Child Benefit stops after 12 weeks in hospital/residential accommodation
- **However**, there's an important exception: if you regularly spend money on Alex while they're in hospital, you can continue to receive Child Benefit even beyond the 12-week limit

- Giving them pocket money
- Paying for extras not covered by the hospital/facility
- Any other regular spending on their behalf

## Child Benefit Eligibility Assessment - Result

### Overall Outcome: **INDETERMINATE** ⚠️

I've completed the assessment for Alex, and unfortunately I cannot give you a definitive yes or no answer at this time. Here's why:

---

### Assessment for Alex:

**Status:** ⚠️ **INDETERMINATE - Further Information Needed**

**Summary:**
You meet most of the eligibility requirements for claiming Child Benefit for Alex:

✅ **What's working in your favor:**
- Alex is 18 and in approved education (qualifying age group)
- Alex doesn't work 24+ hours per week
- Alex doesn't receive qualifying benefits in their own right
- Alex isn't in a disqualifying apprenticeship
- You live in the UK and meet residency requirements
- You contribute £26.05/week towards Alex's upkeep (meeting the responsibility requirement even though Alex doesn't live with you)
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex

❓ **The critical unknown factor:**
- Alex has been in hospital or residential accommodation for **15 weeks**, which exceeds the standard 12-week limit
- Child Benefit normally stops after 12 weeks in hospital/residential accommodation
- **However**, there's an important exception: if you **regularly spend money on Alex** while they're in hospital, you can continue to claim beyond 12 weeks
- Without knowing whether you regularly spend money on Alex during their hospital stay, I cannot determine if you're eligible

---

### What You Need to Do:

**Ask yourself:** Do you regularly spend money on Alex while they are in hospital/residential accommodation? This could include:
- Buying clothes, toiletries, or personal items
- Giving pocket money
- Paying for extras not covered by the facility
- Any other regular spending on their behalf

**If YES** - You should be eligible to continue claiming Child Benefit for Alex

**If NO** - Unfortunately, you would not be eligible because Alex has been in hospital/residential accommodation for more than 12 weeks without you regularly spending on them

### Next Steps:

I recommend contacting HMRC Child Benefit directly to discuss your specific situation:
- **Phone:** 0300 200 3100
- **Website:** https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit
- **Specific guidance on hospital stays:** https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit-for-children-in-hospital-or-care

They can provide a definitive answer based on your exact circumstances.

---

tool_response.description: Determine child's age category for eligibility

tool_response.question: Is the child in approved (non-advanced) education or training?
tool_response.help_text: Approved education: A-levels, T-levels, NVQ Level 3 or below, Scottish Highers/Advanced Highers. Advanced (NOT approved): University degrees, HNC, HND, NVQ Level 4+. Must be full-time (12+ hours/week supervised study).

criteria.must_not_be_married_unless_dependent: Married 16-19 year olds only qualify if financially dependent on claimant

tool_response.question: Is the child working less than 24 hours per week (or not in paid work)?

tool_response.question: Is the child NOT receiving certain benefits in their own right (e.g., ESA, Universal Credit)?
tool_response.help_text: Children receiving Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit in their own right are not eligible

tool_response.question: Is the child NOT in a disqualifying apprenticeship?
tool_response.help_text: Regional rules apply: English apprenticeships (all types) disqualify. Scottish Modern Apprenticeships disqualify. Welsh Foundation Apprenticeships are APPROVED. Other Welsh apprenticeships disqualify.

tool_response.question: Has the child's cumulative time in hospital or residential accommodation exceeded 12 weeks?
tool_response.help_text: Child Benefit continues for up to 12 weeks in hospital/residential accommodation. CUMULATIVE RULE: If child returns within 28 days of leaving, time counts towards 12-week limit. Multiple stays within 28 days are added together.

criteria.calculation_method: Sum all hospital/residential stays. If gap between stays is less than 28 days, count both stays towards cumulative total. If gap is 28+ days, reset counter.
criteria.example: 10 weeks hospital + 15 day gap + 3 weeks hospital = 13 weeks cumulative (exceeds limit)

tool_response.help_text: Exception to 12-week rule if you regularly spend money on child. For hospital abroad, only if they went abroad for treatment and you're back in UK. Partner's spending counts if married/civil partnered and living together.
